payload.headline: Activation for paid_search workspaces fell from 0.2983 to 0.2029 (-0.0954); overall activation also fell, 0.3981 to 0.3797.

cause.text: Activation for paid_search workspaces fell from 0.2983 to 0.2029. Direct (0.4064 to 0.4072) and recap_link (0.4813 to 0.4866) did not move materially.

Organic moved the same direction, from 0.3905 to 0.3848, but is not material (p_value 0.600716). It is kept out of the diagnosis segment because it is indistinguishable from noise and paid_search is the only channel with a material drop.

cause.does_not_prove: That the release is the only contributor.

evidence.quote: The one-time token is marked used the moment anything requests the URL, including an automated prefetch.

cause.text: The drop began at release rel_0612 (2026-02-04). Paid_search activation for signups 2026-02-04 to 2026-02-08 was already 0.2046, versus 0.2973 for 2026-01-26 to 2026-02-03.

cause.does_not_prove: Which exact users hit the broken link.
cause.text: Mechanism is the share step. In paid_search, calendar connect (0.5563 to 0.581) and first meeting (0.4614 to 0.4703) did not fall, so the loss sits between recording a meeting and sharing its recap.

cause.does_not_prove: That these 37 workspaces are paid_search; tickets carry no channel field.

evidence.quote: Our security gateway rewrites and prefetches every link in inbound mail for scanning. Ever since the new share links shipped, every recap we're sent reports as already used by the time we open it.

cause.text: Customers report shared recap links showing as already used, blaming corporate link scanners that prefetch. 37 distinct workspaces filed such tickets from 2026-02-04 to 2026-03-01.

payload.cheapest_test: After rollback, or a fix making the token ignore prefetch requests, compare paid_search activation for new signups against the recent value. Also count recap-link opens returning 'already used' within a minute of sharing.
payload.question: Has anything material changed in the business over the last few weeks, and if so why?
payload.recommendation: Prepare a rollback of rel_0612's one-time share links, or make the token ignore automated prefetches. The PM is away, so this is prepare-only and needs PM approval. Flag as urgent: material change in a key metric.

ruled_out.does_not_prove: That nothing provider-specific is also present.
ruled_out.text: Microsoft calendar provider as the cause: Microsoft activation fell overall (0.3917 to 0.3599), but inside Microsoft only paid_search moved materially (0.2949 to 0.1719). Google paid_search fell too (0.3025 to 0.2178). The drop follows channel, not provider.

ruled_out.does_not_prove: That the email change had no effect on opens.

evidence.quote: Copy only; no change to the share link, the share flow, or any other behavior.

ruled_out.text: Release rel_0702 (recap email subject line, 2026-02-20) is ruled out: it shipped after the drop began and is copy-only.

size.method: activation gap x conversion gap (activated vs not) x trials per week in the segment x ARR per paid workspace

unknowns: Why paid_search is hit and other channels are not.
Tickets carry no channel field, so the channel mix of the 37 workspaces is Unknown.
The flag state could not be read (permission denied).
would_change_if: Share-event logs show paid_search shares succeed at the same rate as before rel_0612.
Activation does not recover within a full 7-day cohort window after the fix.
